exposure: Heart disease status (congenital and acquired heart disease vs. control)
cohort: The participants were 77 women with congenital and acquired heart disease and 154 control women, with data collected from their first and second pregnancies.
finding: Women with mild to moderate heart disease experienced similar rates of cardiac, obstetric, and perinatal complications in consecutive pregnancies, and unlike control women, their babies did not show an increase in median birthweight in the second pregnancy.
birth_weight: Median birthweight for control groups was 3308g (first) and 3519g (second); for heart disease groups it was 3014g (first) and 3133g (second).
